correctness.rationale: For any finite poset with n>=2, the augmented Hasse covers give precisely the minimal facets (standard order-polytope theorem). Pairwise equalities on two distinct covers either create a single three-point block or two two-point blocks; contraction is exactly codimension two iff no extra forced equality/cycle. For consecutive edges a<b<c the only obstruction is a fourth interval point between a,c; for disjoint edges (a,b),(c,d), the only quotient cycle requires both cross comparisons a<d,c<b. Common-source/target edges are compatible. These cases give R=binom(F,2)-Bchain-Bcross. The outward normals e_a-e_b (formal bottom/top coordinates 0) have dot products yielding only pi/4,pi/3,pi/2,2pi/3 with the claimed Tboundary,Tinterior,U and remaining right-angle counts. I independently enumerated 1,098 increasing-labelled edge-mask posets n=2..5 and, for each, compared every facet pair against the rank of all tight 0/1 order-vertices, including the exact angle class; all passed. This finite check corroborates, but the cover-partition proof supplies the all-poset statement.

value.rationale: All finite posets and their Euclidean order polytopes form a foundational natural class. A finite local Hasse-diagram recipe that simultaneously characterizes ridge nonincidence and four exact angle multiplicities is structural and useful for combinatorial and metric polyhedral questions, especially crossed-cover obstructions beyond tree or chain cases, rather than a routine single-instance numerical computation.
